clinician.trajectory_summary: A 19-year-old man presented with severe epigastric pain, vomiting, and weight loss refractory to H. pylori treatment. Abdominal CT with contrast showed diffuse gastric wall thickening with mucosal enhancement and lymphadenopathy. The patient was afebrile and hemodynamically stable on admission with negative initial microbiologic testing (HIV, COVID-19, Quanti-FERON, CMV NAAT, blood and urine cultures). Upper endoscopy demonstrated congested, erythematous, eroded, friable, nodular, scalloped gastric mucosa and erythematous duodenal mucosa, consistent with severe gastritis and duodenitis. However, histopathology and microbiology results from biopsy specimens were not documented. The clinical, imaging, and endoscopic findings align with phlegmonous gastritis and duodenitis despite absence of systemic infection signs and negative initial infectious screens.
